name: Nadia Black
life: “I still remember a bride apologizing for her elbows.” On Sunday, near the approach to Seabright Court, Nadia likes to watch the beach traffic thin enough for workers going the other way.
voice: I am tired of brides apologizing to the glass. I drape it until they tell me they're ready.
appearance: Nadia has close-cropped dark curls, a small notch in the left eyebrow, and a favorite piece of clothing, a rust-colored canvas coat. It usually goes with a seam let out by a narrow strip of contrasting fabric. When somebody else has the floor, Nadia looks toward the door whenever a name is called.
personality: Nadia loves an audience until a private hurt enters the room. Then the performer disappears and someone very good at getting other people through a door takes over.
agenda: To uncover the mirror when the bride asks.
family: Santiago Wells is Nadia’s cousin. Nadia picks the meeting place. Santiago sets the time to leave. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *Three minutes at the bridge*, Santiago says, “I used to travel in complete silence. I asked the others to let me have one quiet morning a week.”
connections: Ashley Byrd (tailor). They put the mirror at a height that lets a seated customer choose when to look.

reactions.situation: The mirror owner wants it back during a fitting
reactions.response: Nadia asks the two shops for enough time to finish the fitting in privacy.

reactions.situation: A stranger offers money to cut ahead of an exhausted neighbor
reactions.response: Nadia keeps the neighbor's place and finds out whether the stranger needs a different kind of help.

reactions.response: Nadia offers one about their own embarrassment instead.
